Two men wearing striped textile body cloths, one holding a staff. In the distance can be seen the hut of a homestead, and car tyre tracks are clearly visible on the road near their feet. It seems that Evans-Pritchard visited a Shilluk village briefly during one of his trips to the Nuer, probably near the Doleib Hill missionary station on the Sobat River (roughly six miles from its confluence with the White Nile), established in 1902 by the American Presbytarian Mission and after 1925 run by Rev. J. A. Heasty, seen in one of the images.

A squatting man plucking a lyre with two other men with a spear and club, sitting on the ground alongside, and a small hut just beyond. Outside the hut is a tressle table with some ?bedding folded on it, and a man in overalls walks towards it. It seems that Evans-Pritchard visited a Shilluk village briefly during one of his trips to the Nuer, probably near the Doleib Hill missionary station on the Sobat River (roughly six miles from its confluence with the White Nile), established in 1902 by the American Presbytarian Mission and after 1925 run by Rev. J. A. Heasty, seen in one of the images.

The Rev. J. A. Heasty of the American Presbytarian Mission with his son, who was posted to the newly established Doleib Hill mission station on the Sobat River (roughly six miles from its confluence with the White Nile) in 1925 as a specialist in the teaching of English language. The station was founded in 1902 to provide industrial and agricultural training, a focus encouraged by the British administration. With an increasing demand for English language education from local elites however, the APM responded with another station at Nasir on the Sobat river.

A Shilluk man standing next to the hut of a homestead, apparently performing a spear-dance for the camera, with others sitting in the shade of a wind-break nearby. Other huts of the village can be seen beyond. J. A. Heasty, seen in one of the images.

Some Shilluk women in the distance with large water pots standing on the bank of the Sobat River having collected water. A long rope stretches across the bank into the water in the foreground, perhaps a mooring for the boat that Evans-Pritchard was travelling on along the river. A very distant view from a steam boat on the Sobat or White Nile River of five separate groupings of Shilluk huts in a treeless plain. It seems that Evans-Pritchard visited a Shilluk village briefly during one of his trips to the Nuer, probably the Doleib Hill missionary station on the Sobat River (roughly six miles from its confluence with the White Nile), established in 1902 by the American Presbytarian Mission and after 1925 run by Rev. J. A. Heasty, seen in one of the images.
Three men posed for the camera holding spears and clubs, wearing textiles and arm and neck ornaments. Two are wearing headdresses of differing types as well as a long-fringed leather arm bands.

A large group of Shilluk people at the burial ceremony of a person in Omdurman. According to the Seligman's (who almost certainly took this image on their first voyage up the Nile in 1909-10) dancing women bearing spears went round and round the grave, whilst others played bells and drums. This scene shows the attendance of men in war regalia, spears and shields, along with a tribal flag.

Looking across the river from a steam boat to the huts of a Shilluk village and a few palm trees. Alongside the domed huts can be seen circular enclosures for eating and socializing, as well as a smaller enclosure, possibly marking a gravesite. A number of villagers are at the riverside.

Looking from the side of a riverboat as it comes in to moor at the landing stage, with Shilluk people on the bank and in the shallows meeting it. Two men have taken the anchor some distance away and are attempting to fix it into the ground. In the foreground a Shilluk man with sculpted hair is about to hand a skin bag with wooden objects inside to someone on board.
Shilluk men in Malakal on their way to a dance.
Shilluk people holding flags making their way to the football stadium during the ceremonies held there in July 2006 to mark the first anniversary of the death of John Garang.
A Shilluk cattle herding village located on an island in the river. The huts of the homesteds are formed into a circle surrounding a central cattle pen area in the centre.
Three Shilluk youths wearing neck and head ornaments seated in a homestead.
A posed line of Shilluk youths wearing ornaments and pointing spears towards the camera.
A full length portrait of a Shilluk youth wearing ornaments and holding two large spears, one with tassel decoration.
A Shilluk homestead showing several huts and two youths walking in the foreground.
An upper body portrait of an initiated Shilluk youth with white hair treatment and feather ornaments in it.
A full length portrait of a Shilluk youth with elaborate coiffure and holding a short stabbing spear.
Portrait of a Shilluk youth sitting on the ground, possibly holding a pipe.
A profile portrait of Shilluk man with coiffure and arm ornament.
A view of a hut and fence silhouetted against an early morning/evening sky.
A view of a group of young men and boys wearing coloured shoulder cloths. Some men have highlighted the scars on their foreheads in white. Some men wear long beaded bracelets. They carry long staves.
Dark silhouette of people under a tree.

A portrait of respected chief Kwan Yurath Bol with chiefs under a tree. He wears an ivory necklace. It is dark. Kwan Yurath Bol was called to the village of Debalo, where the Reth elect was hiding, to mediate a dispute between chiefs and government police. See 2009.6.65 to 2009.6.70; 2009.6.110; 2009.6.321; 2009.6.415 to 2009.6.423; and 2009.6.500.
A view of a group of warriors against a dark sky, carrying tall staves.

Portrait of the head and shoulders of a Shilluk man (probably a chief) looking at the camera against a dark background. He wears a mustard coloured cap, white bead (shell?) necklace and carried two thick staves, possibly spears.

A view of the Reth elect (centre right with beret) standing with warriors carrying maize sticks, in front of a stockaded compound. This is probably in Debalo before the Reth moves to the river bed where the mock battles will take place. See 2009.6.180 to 2009.6.187.
Possibly a view of the roofs of the Reth's compound, late sunset.
A dramatic view of the sunset across the landscape.

A group of Shilluk men, some chiefs, wearing pinkish cloth toga-like garments stand beside a groups of huts. They are with a younger woman who looks at the camera. The man on the right wears a green fez style hat, green scarf and white beaded necklace. He carries a covered sword.
A view from afar of the Shilluk capital Fashoda showing the scrub landscape of the area.
Landscape view of the Reth's compound Akurwick seen against the setting/rising sun.

Portrait of a Shilluk man (possibly a chief), with an orange cap rubbing sticks together to make fire. As Debalo is an important location during the ceremonies of the making of the Reth it is likely this is part of the rituals. See 2009.6.140. Spears are lined up behind him and he wears a white bead necklace and a blue necklace with silver pendant. He kneels on a pair of rubber shoes.

A young woman sits with closed eyes, her arms outstretched. The spiritual aspects of Nyikang are seen as powerful. This is probably the effect on her after the effigy of Nyikang and/or Dak has blessed her. See 2009.6.116; 2009.6.127 and 2009.6.143 to 2009.6 145.

Shilluk children posing for photograph, near the Nile River
A Shilluk girl of the Sudd region
A Shilluk girl of the Sudd region facing away from camera, near the Nile River
